state.claim: At the closing commit, the report records `status: passed` for all seven required assertions — `dev_gates.exit_zero`, `corpus.proved_corpus_c`, `corpus_c.no_new_errors`, `public_corpora.no_drift`, `mutants.every_decision_accused`, `instruments.drift_detectors_fire`, `source.untouched_after_mutants`. corpus-c no longer exists on any machine, so `corpus.proved_corpus_c` and `corpus_c.no_new_errors` pass the only way they still can: gate d's own status is `SKIP` for the retired corpus, and every baselined public corpus matches its own baseline exactly, which `corpus_c.public_corpora_matched_baseline: true` in the report confirms.

relation.instructions: `claim` is a sentence the repository makes about the commit it closes. `evidence` is the gate report produced by running the gates on that commit. Does the evidence support the claim? Judge only what the evidence shows.

criteria.supports: the evidence contains every effect the claim promises
criteria.contradicts: the evidence shows at least one of the promised effects did not happen
criteria.says_nothing: the evidence is silent about at least one effect the claim promises
